title: Big-Pot Savory Oats
subtitle: A practical station breakfast that scales from 4 to 12.
description: A single pot of oats that tastes like a real breakfast, not diet culture. We finish with salt, butter, and a sensible topping bar so everyone can customize without slowing the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Big-Pot Savory Oats in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Simmer the oats
steps.instruction: Bring liquid and salt to a boil. Stir in oats; reduce to a simmer. Cook until creamy, stirring often so nothing sticks. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Finish savory
steps.instruction: Stir in butter. Taste and adjust salt. Keep covered on low while the crew builds bowls. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Set the topping bar
steps.instruction: Lay out cheese, green onions, hot sauce, and soft eggs. Let everyone build without crowding the pot. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Serve and hold
steps.instruction: Hold the pot on the lowest heat with a splash of water if it thickens. Refill toppings as needed. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
